attachments.landmark_a: posteromedial aspect of lateral femoral condyle

bands.name: Anteromedial bundle
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to anterior tibial translation; tautest bundle in flexion
bands.function_note: The bundle most commonly reconstructed as a single-bundle graft when double-bundle reconstruction is not performed.
bands.source: Girgis FG, Marshall JL, Monajem A (1975) 'The cruciate ligaments of the knee joint: anatomical, functional and experimental analysis.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 106:216-231 -- classic cadaveric description of the ACL's anteromedial/posterolateral bundle and PCL's anterolateral/posteromedial bundle reciprocal-tension architecture.

bands.name: Posterolateral bundle
bands.mechanical_role: contributes rotational stability, particularly resisting anterior translation and internal rotation near full extension
bands.function_note: Reciprocally taut with the anteromedial bundle: this bundle slackens in flexion as the AM bundle tightens, and vice versa near extension.
bands.source: Girgis FG, Marshall JL, Monajem A (1975) 'The cruciate ligaments of the knee joint: anatomical, functional and experimental analysis.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 106:216-231 -- classic cadaveric description of the ACL's anteromedial/posterolateral bundle and PCL's anterolateral/posteromedial bundle reciprocal-tension architecture.

function: The knee's primary restraint against anterior tibial translation (per selective-cutting biomechanical studies) and a major contributor to rotational stability; its rupture is among the most common major ligament injuries in sport.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Girgis FG, Marshall JL, Monajem A (1975) 'The cruciate ligaments of the knee joint: anatomical, functional and experimental analysis.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 106:216-231 -- classic cadaveric description of the ACL's anteromedial/posterolateral bundle and PCL's anterolateral/posteromedial bundle reciprocal-tension architecture.; Butler DL, Noyes FR, Grood ES (1980) 'Ligamentous restraints to anterior-posterior drawer in the human knee: a biomechanical study.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 62(2):259-270 -- ACL identified as the primary restraint to anterior tibial translation (PCL to posterior translation) via selective cutting studies.

attachments.landmark_a: anterolateral aspect of medial femoral condyle

bands.name: Anterolateral bundle
bands.mechanical_role: the larger, stronger bundle; primary restraint to posterior tibial translation, tautest in flexion
bands.function_note: Roughly twice the cross-sectional area of the posteromedial bundle -- the PCL's dominant functional bundle.
bands.source: Girgis FG, Marshall JL, Monajem A (1975) 'The cruciate ligaments of the knee joint: anatomical, functional and experimental analysis.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 106:216-231 -- classic cadaveric description of the ACL's anteromedial/posterolateral bundle and PCL's anterolateral/posteromedial bundle reciprocal-tension architecture.

bands.name: Posteromedial bundle
bands.function_note: Smaller and reciprocally tensioned relative to the anterolateral bundle, similar in principle to the ACL's two-bundle reciprocal pattern.
bands.source: Girgis FG, Marshall JL, Monajem A (1975) 'The cruciate ligaments of the knee joint: anatomical, functional and experimental analysis.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 106:216-231 -- classic cadaveric description of the ACL's anteromedial/posterolateral bundle and PCL's anterolateral/posteromedial bundle reciprocal-tension architecture.

function: The knee's primary restraint against posterior tibial translation; on average stronger and less frequently injured in isolation than the ACL.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Girgis FG, Marshall JL, Monajem A (1975) 'The cruciate ligaments of the knee joint: anatomical, functional and experimental analysis.' Clin Orthop Relat Res 106:216-231 -- classic cadaveric description of the ACL's anteromedial/posterolateral bundle and PCL's anterolateral/posteromedial bundle reciprocal-tension architecture.; Butler DL, Noyes FR, Grood ES (1980) 'Ligamentous restraints to anterior-posterior drawer in the human knee: a biomechanical study.' J Bone Joint Surg Am 62(2):259-270 -- ACL identified as the primary restraint to anterior tibial translation (PCL to posterior translation) via selective cutting studies.

attachments.landmark_b: medial tibial shaft, ~5cm below joint line

bands.name: Superficial layer

attachments.landmark_b: medial tibial metaphysis, deep to pes anserinus tendons

bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to valgus stress at the knee
bands.function_note: A long, flat, extracapsular band -- the structure most commonly meant by 'the MCL' in clinical use.
bands.source: Woo SL, Abramowitch SD, Kilger R, Liang R (2006) 'Biomechanics of knee ligaments: injury, healing, and repair.' J Biomech 39(1):1-20 -- knee ligament (ACL/PCL/MCL) structure-function review, representative failure load/stiffness figures.

bands.name: Deep layer (meniscofemoral + meniscotibial portions)

attachments.landmark_a: medial epicondyle, deep to the superficial layer
attachments.landmark_b: medial meniscus periphery and tibial plateau rim

bands.mechanical_role: secondary valgus restraint; anchors the medial meniscus's periphery to the capsule
bands.function_note: Anatomically a true capsular thickening distinct from the superficial (extracapsular) layer, and the direct anchor of the medial meniscus's outer margin -- the structural reason a torn MCL is frequently accompanied by a medial meniscal tear ('unhappy triad' with the ACL).
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The knee's primary medial (valgus) stabilizer, working in two structurally distinct layers.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Woo SL, Abramowitch SD, Kilger R, Liang R (2006) 'Biomechanics of knee ligaments: injury, healing, and repair.' J Biomech 39(1):1-20 -- knee ligament (ACL/PCL/MCL) structure-function review, representative failure load/stiffness figures.

bands.name: Fibular collateral ligament
bands.mechanical_role: primary restraint to varus stress at the knee
bands.function_note: A round, cord-like (not flat/broad like the MCL) extracapsular structure, separated from the joint capsule by a fat-filled space, and unlike the MCL has no direct attachment to the lateral meniscus.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The knee's primary lateral (varus) stabilizer; part of the posterolateral corner complex together with the popliteus tendon and popliteofibular ligament.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

bands.name: Patellar ligament
bands.mechanical_role: transmits quadriceps extensor force to the tibia; the patella functions as a sesamoid bone within this tendon-ligament continuum
bands.function_note: Terminologically a 'ligament' (bone-to-bone, patella-to-tibia) but functionally and developmentally the continuation of the quadriceps femoris tendon distal to the patella -- the patella itself is the largest sesamoid bone in the body, embedded within this single musculotendinous-ligamentous chain.
bands.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The distal continuation of the quadriceps mechanism; a common autograft source (bone-patellar tendon-bone) for ACL reconstruction given its robust bone-to-bone attachments.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
